description:
The agent-facing bridge presents the profile commands in their renamed vocabulary, so an agent reading the tool surface meets the same description an adopter does.

## Background

The bridge generates its tool surface at every process start from the command schema, so the tools' names and arguments follow the renamed surface with no edit. Two checked-in files do not: three curated tool descriptions describe the profile commands as operating on packages embedded in the connected binary, and the bridge's own coverage asserts over that surface.

The descriptions are shipped adopter-facing text, so they are the substance of this change; the coverage assertion follows them.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No curated tool description presents a profile package as embedded in the binary.
- [hard] REQ-02: The curated descriptions match what the renamed commands do, including reading a package from a repository location.
- [hard] REQ-03: The bridge's coverage passes against the renamed surface, with no tool changing name or arguments.
- [hard] REQ-04: No schema artefact is checked in; the surface is still generated at process start.

## Notes

The instruction block's own vocabulary is a separate entry's subject; the two touch different parts of the same curation file and neither edits the other's lines.
title: Follow the renamed profile surface on the agent-facing bridge
